package_info.package_manager: N/A (malware distributed via phishing and exploits, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: SmokeLoader is a modular malware loader that delivers and executes a variety of malicious plugins designed to steal credentials, exfiltrate sensitive data, inject code into legitimate processes, and maintain persistence on infected Windows systems. It leverages phishing, exploits, and multi-stage loaders to evade detection and maximize impact.

execution_context.file_location: malicious Microsoft Office document (CVE-2017-0199 or CVE-2017-11882)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: OLE2-embedded link object or equation editor shellcode that downloads and executes a remote VBS file using URLDownloadToFile.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the document is opened, the embedded exploit triggers, downloads a VBS file from a remote server, and executes it, enabling the next stage of malware delivery.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Office documents should not download and execute code from the internet upon opening.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal Office documents do not contain hidden objects or shellcode that fetches and runs remote scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated document templates may fetch data, but not execute arbitrary code.
key_indicators: Automatic download and execution of remote scripts

execution_context.file_location: HTA file or VBS file (downloaded by exploit)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Obfuscated VBS script that decodes and executes PowerShell code to download another VBS file (AndeLoader).
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution, the VBS script decodes embedded PowerShell, which downloads the next-stage VBS loader, continuing the infection chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated scripts that download and execute further code are a hallmark of malware loaders.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate VBS/HTA files do not typically contain multi-layered obfuscation and staged payload delivery.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some enterprise scripts may use PowerShell for automation, but not for multi-stage payload delivery.
key_indicators: PowerShell used to download and execute further scripts

execution_context.file_location: AndeLoader VBS file (downloaded by previous stage)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Deobfuscated PowerShell code that downloads a steganographic image, extracts base64-encoded injector, decodes it, and executes dnlib.IO.Home.VAI method with arguments including the SmokeLoader payload URL.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the loader downloads a steganographic image, extracts and decodes the embedded injector, and executes it with parameters to fetch and inject the SmokeLoader payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of steganography to hide payloads and dynamic code execution is a strong indicator of malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate scripts do not use steganography to hide and execute code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Steganography is rarely used in legitimate enterprise automation.
key_indicators: Dynamic code execution with attacker-controlled arguments

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Class.Start method: Combines VBS files, writes persistence to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, downloads and injects SmokeLoader into RegAsm.exe by creating a suspended process, writing payload to memory, and modifying thread context to point to SmokeLoader entry point.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the injector establishes persistence by modifying the registry, downloads the SmokeLoader payload, and injects it into a legitimate Windows process for execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Registry persistence and process injection are classic malware techniques for stealth and persistence.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not inject code into system processes or modify registry autorun keys without user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate updaters use registry autorun, but not process injection.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into RegAsm.exe (or explorer.exe for plugins)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SmokeLoader main module: Connects to C2 server, downloads plugin configurations and encrypted plugin payloads, injects plugins into explorer.exe or other target processes using process hollowing and shellcode.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, SmokeLoader contacts its C2, receives plugin payloads, and injects them into legitimate processes for further malicious activity.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: C2 communication, plugin-based architecture, and process injection are all advanced malware behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not inject arbitrary code into system processes or download and execute untrusted plugins.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is classic malware loader behavior.

execution_context.file_location: Injected into browsers, email clients, FTP clients, explorer.exe

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Plugins (1-9): API hooking code that intercepts credential storage/access APIs (e.g., vaultcli.dll, registry, SQLite files, wininet.dll, ws2_32.dll, user32.dll), extracts credentials, cookies, autofill data, clipboard content, and exfiltrates to C2.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, injected plugins hook sensitive APIs in target processes, steal credentials and user data, and send it to the attacker's C2 server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: API hooking for credential theft and data exfiltration is a hallmark of advanced infostealers.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate plugins or extensions do not hook system APIs to steal and exfiltrate user data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Security software may hook APIs for monitoring, but not for exfiltration.
key_indicators: API hooking in browsers and email clients
Exfiltration of credentials and sensitive data

attack_chain.action: Victim receives phishing email with malicious Office document exploiting CVE-2017-0199 or CVE-2017-11882.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initial code execution and download of VBS loader

attack_chain.action: Malicious VBS/HTA script executes, decodes PowerShell, and downloads AndeLoader.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of AndeLoader and download of steganographic payload

attack_chain.action: AndeLoader downloads steganographic image, extracts and decodes injector, and executes it with parameters for SmokeLoader.
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of injector and download of SmokeLoader

attack_chain.action: Injector establishes persistence, downloads SmokeLoader, and injects it into RegAsm.exe.
SmokeLoader connects to C2, downloads plugin configurations and payloads, and injects plugins into explorer.exe or other targets.
Plugins hook APIs in browsers, email clients, FTP clients, and explorer.exe to steal credentials, cookies, clipboard data, and exfiltrate to C2.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration and completion of attack objectives

behavioral_signatures: Office document execution triggers download and execution of remote scripts
Obfuscated VBS/HTA scripts decoding and running PowerShell
Registry Run key modification for persistence
Process injection into RegAsm.exe or explorer.exe
API hooking in browsers, email clients, and FTP clients
Network communication with known C2 IPs/domains
file_indicators: Office documents exploiting CVE-2017-0199 or CVE-2017-11882
Obfuscated VBS/HTA files in user temp or downloads
Registry key: HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run with suspicious VBS path
Injected or hollowed RegAsm.exe or explorer.exe processes
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/HTTPS requests to attacker-controlled servers for payload and plugin delivery
Exfiltration of data to remote C2 endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Office documents that trigger downloads and execution of scripts, especially those exploiting known vulnerabilities. Detect obfuscated VBS/HTA/PowerShell activity, especially multi-stage downloads and steganographic payload extraction. Alert on registry Run key modifications pointing to suspicious scripts. Monitor for process injection into RegAsm.exe or explorer.exe, and for API hooking in browsers and email clients. Correlate with known C2 IPs and unusual outbound traffic patterns.
